test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is true according to the First Law of Motion?

options.text: A person continues to move forward when a car stops suddenly.
A car accelerates when the engine is started.
A stone falling freely under gravity.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A person continues to move forward when a car stops suddenly.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The First Law of Motion**, also known as Newton's First Law or the Law of Inertia, states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• When a car stops suddenly, a person inside the car continues to move forward due to **inertia**. This is because the body tends to maintain its state of motion unless an external force (like a seatbelt) acts on it. Hence, this statement is correct.
 
• A rocket launching upward does not directly illustrate the First Law of Motion but is instead an example of **Newton's Third Law**, which involves action and reaction forces. Hence, this statement is incorrect.
 
• A car accelerating when the engine is started demonstrates the application of a net external force, which aligns with Newton's Second Law of Motion (Force = mass × acceleration). Hence, this statement is incorrect.
 
• A stone falling freely under gravity illustrates Newton's Second Law since the acceleration due to gravity acts on the stone. It is not an example of the First Law. Hence, this statement is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion (Law of Inertia):**

 
 
• An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion continues in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force.
 
• This law emphasizes the concept of **inertia**, which is the resistance of an object to changes in its state of motion.
 
 
 
• **Inertia:**
 
 
• Inertia is the property of a body due to which it resists any change in its state of rest or uniform motion.
 
• Example: When a train suddenly stops, passengers inside experience a forward motion because their bodies resist the sudden change in motion.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:**
 
 
• This law states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object times its acceleration (F = ma).
 
• Example: A car accelerating demonstrates the application of a net force.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion:**
 
 
• This law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• Example: The upward motion of a rocket is due to the downward expulsion of gases, which creates an equal and opposite reaction force.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Newton's First Law:**
 
 
• Seatbelts in cars are designed to counter inertia, preventing passengers from continuing forward motion during sudden stops.
 
• Tablecloth trick: Quickly pulling a tablecloth from under dishes without moving them illustrates inertia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Inertia:**

 
 
• It explains why passengers in a moving vehicle lurch forward when the vehicle comes to a sudden stop.
 
• It is crucial in understanding the dynamics of motion in various systems, from vehicles to celestial bodies.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Newton's First Law was influenced by the earlier work of **Galileo Galilei**, who studied motion and the principle of inertia.
 
• Isaac Newton formulated the laws of motion in his seminal work **"Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica"**, published in **1687**.
